content.text:
Auth0 login is set up in your app, and the app builds without errors. I haven't tried a real login yet.

**Auth0 side:**
- The onboarding tool created a single-page app called **HackWestern13** on your tenant `dev-5dn87rsiwz8zmm6f.us.auth0.com`. It saved the domain and client ID to `.env.local`.
- The quickstart tool registered `http://localhost:5173/` as the allowed address to return to after login and logout, and as an allowed web origin.
- It also automatically turned on the setting that skips Auth0's confirmation prompt for addresses it can't verify, like localhost.
- Single-page apps don't use a client secret. If you ever need the app's full settings, they're in the [Auth0 dashboard](https://manage.auth0.com/dashboard/us/dev-5dn87rsiwz8zmm6f/applications/REDACTED/settings).

**App side:** the repo only had a README, so I built a small Vite + React app at the repo root instead of cloning Auth0's sample into a subfolder.
- `src/main.jsx` wraps the app in `Auth0Provider` and reads the domain and client ID from `.env.local`, so they aren't written into the code.
- `src/App.jsx` has Signup, Login and Logout buttons and shows the logged-in user's profile.
- `npm run dev` always runs on port 5173. If that port is taken it fails instead of switching ports, because a different port wouldn't match the login address Auth0 expects.
- I added a `.gitignore` so `node_modules`, `.env.local` and the Auth0 tool's local files stay out of git.

To try it, run `npm run dev`, open http://localhost:5173 and click **Signup**.

During install, npm skipped a setup script for `browser-tabs-lock`, a package the Auth0 library depends on. It doesn't seem to affect the build.

Nothing is committed yet. Tell me if you want me to commit it.

content.text:
I found it. **The problem is a bug in TinyFish's CLI, not your Claude Code.** To decide whether Claude Code can take an API key, TinyFish runs `claude mcp --help` and looks for a `--header` option. In your version, that option is listed only under `claude mcp add --help`, so the check fails and TinyFish wrongly tells you to update. Your Claude Code does support it.

You can skip `tinyfish connect` and add the server yourself, the same way TinyFish would have. In its setup code, TinyFish registers Claude Code with your key in an `X-API-Key` header. Run this with your full key (starting with `sk-tinyfish--`, no period at the end):

```
! claude mcp add --scope user --transport http tinyfish https://agent.tinyfish.ai/mcp --header "X-API-Key: sk-tinyfish--<rest of your key>"
```

Then:
1. Run `! claude mcp list` to check that `tinyfish` shows up and connects.
2. Start a new Claude Code session. The tools only load at startup.
3. In that new session, ask me to run `tinyfish doctor --pretty` and find today's top Hacker News story.

This adds only the MCP server. `connect` would also have installed TinyFish's skills, but those are extras. The tools should work without them.

You might want to report the version check to TinyFish. It's in their `harness-spec.js`: the Claude Code check looks for `--header` in `claude mcp --help`, but it only appears in `claude mcp add --help`.

TinyFish is set up and working. I used its CLI to pull the Hacker News front page, and the #1 story right now is **"Derek Lowe: Detonating a Pile of Lead Azide"** (science.org, 215 points, 122 comments, posted 3 hours ago).

**Agents connected:** Claude Code only, and it was the only coding agent on your Mac. `claude mcp list` shows `tinyfish ✔ Connected`, and `tinyfish doctor` passes every check, including your key and a test call to TinyFish.

**Browser sign-ins still needed:** none. The connection uses your API key, so there's no browser login left to do.

**What I couldn't finish:**
- **The automatic setup didn't connect Claude Code.** TinyFish's `connect` command wrongly decided your Claude Code was too old to take a key. Its check looks for the `--header` option in the wrong help screen. We added the server by hand with `claude mcp add` instead.
- **TinyFish's skills aren't installed.** `connect` would normally add these too, but they're optional; the tools work without them.
- **The TinyFish tools aren't in this session.** Claude Code only loads them at startup, so I did the Hacker News test with the `tinyfish` command instead. Start a new session to use the tools directly.

Your key is now in this conversation's history and saved in `~/.claude.json`, so consider rotating it if that's a concern. If you do, run `tinyfish auth set` with the new key, then the `claude mcp add` command again.
